Leber hereditary optic neuropathy: The patient's symptoms of lifelong uncorrectable visual acuity and color vision impairment, combined with the father's similar symptoms and lack of consanguinity, suggest a hereditary cause. The fundus examination and visual field testing results also support this diagnosis.
Retinitis pigmentosa: The patient's symptoms of progressive blurred central vision and color vision defects, along with the fundus examination and OCT results showing thinning of the outer nuclear layer, are consistent with retinitis pigmentosa. The family history also supports this diagnosis.
